records.title: Senior Manager, Regional Food Safety Quality Assurance (FSQA)

postedPay.title: Senior Manager, Regional Food Safety Quality Assurance (FSQA)

records.description:
**Purpose**
Dole Packaged Foods is a purpose led organization that is a champion of accessible fruit nutrition and builds a brighter future for people through the goodness of fruit.
 
 
At Dole, our culture is uniquely driven by core Values. Our commitment to these Values transforms our work into a meaningful journey toward a brighter future together. Here, you'll be part of a respectful, inclusive culture that deeply values our colleagues, customers, and global communities. We strive for excellence, empowering each other to confidently overcome challenges, continuously learn, and achieve world-class results. Guided by unwavering integrity, our actions consistently reflect our commitment to always doing what's right, fostering lasting trust and strong relationships. Through a spirit of collaboration, we cultivate positivity, generosity, and genuine teamwork, enabling collective success toward our One Dole Purpose. Our innovative spirit leads directly to meaningful outcomes and business success.
 
 
The Senior Manager, Regional Food Safety & Quality Assurance (FSQA) provides leadership and direction for food safety and quality across the North America region. Serving as a key partner to regional business and Supply Chain leadership, this role oversees regional and site FSQA execution, drives performance and continuous improvement, and serves as a primary Quality representative for customers and key business partners.
 
 
Working collaboratively across Operations, Supply Chain and Global FSQR, the Senior Manager helps translate company priorities into effective execution while strengthening food safety and quality capability throughout the region. This is a highly visible leadership role for an experienced professional who enjoys developing people, solving complex problems and influencing how Quality supports the business.
 
 
This role provides flexibility to work in a hybrid environment of home and our Westlake Village, CA office. (Hybrid is defined as 3 times per week in the office).
 
 
**Responsibilities**
**Primary Accountabilities:**
**Regional FSQA Leadership & Execution**

* Lead food safety and quality execution across North America, providing oversight to regional and site FSQA teams and serving as the primary FSQA partner to regional business and Supply Chain leadership.
* Monitor significant food safety and quality risks, performance gaps and corrective actions, ensuring effective execution, follow-through and appropriate escalation.
* Lead, coach and develop FSQA personnel while strengthening food safety and quality culture, capability and accountability across the region.

**Program Deployment & Capability Building**

* Lead regional implementation and reinforcement of company food safety and quality programs, standards and requirements including training and capability building across applicable functions.
* Coordinate regional food safety and quality incidents, ensuring appropriate assessment, communication, escalation and corrective action in partnership with relevant stakeholders.
* Partner with Global FSQR subject-matter experts to address technical and capability needs and support development of regional or facility SOPs, protocols and other supporting documentation.

**Customer, Business & Supply Chain Partnership**

* Serve as the primary North America Quality Representative for customers including strategic customer relationships, audits, inquiries and quality-related issues.
* Partner with Supply Chain, Operations, Commercial, Procurement, R&D and other functions to integrate food safety and quality requirements into business activities, commercialization and change initiatives.
* Coordinate regional FSQA activities involving suppliers, third-party manufacturers, warehousing and transportation in partnership with the appropriate Global FSQR teams.

**Performance & Continuous Improvement**

* Drive regional FSQA performance through KPIs, scorecards, trend analysis and management reporting, providing appropriate visibility to regional leadership and Global FSQR.
* Identify systemic risks, recurring issues and improvement opportunities and drive effective corrective and preventive actions across the region.
* Manage regional FSQA resources and priorities to support business needs, strengthen execution and continuously improve food safety and quality performance.
* Other duties as assigned

**Qualifications**
**Experience, Knowledge, & Skills You Bring:**

* 8+ years of progressive experience in food safety, quality assurance or related food manufacturing disciplines, including demonstrated leadership responsibility.
* Strong knowledge of food safety and quality management systems, HACCP/Preventive Controls, GMPs, GFSI-recognized certification schemes and applicable U.S./Canada food regulations.
* Experience working across manufacturing, Supply Chain and cross-functional business environments.
* Demonstrated ability to lead through influence and work effectively across organizational boundaries.
* Experience managing customer quality relationships and communicating effectively with senior business leaders.
* Strong understanding of incident management, risk assessment, corrective and preventive action, and continuous improvement principles.
* Strong analytical and communication skills with the ability to translate technical issues and performance data into practical business actions.
* Demonstrated ability to coach and develop technical professionals and build effective cross-functional relationships.

**What You’ll Need to Succeed:**

* Passionate about a purpose driven career
* Committed to fostering inclusive environments that support employee development and well-being
* Sets clear expectations, encourages innovation, and drives continuous improvement
* Models and coaches towards transparency and integrity in decision-making
* Effectively facilitates cross-team communication and teamwork

**Education & Certification:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Food Science, Microbiology, Biology, Chemistry or Life Sciences is required.
* Advanced degree preferred but not required.
* HACCP and/or Preventive Controls Qualified Individual (PCQI) training strongly preferred.
* Relevant GFSI, auditing, food safety or quality certifications are beneficial.

**Physical Requirements:**

* Ability to sit and use the computer for extended periods of time; ability to answer phones and use a variety of office equipment; ability to lift 15 pounds and reach overhead.

**Travel Requirements:**

* Approximately 30-40%, including travel to company facilities, customers, and business partners as required.

**All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, color, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, or on the basis of disability.**
**For Jobs Based In California**
Hiring Pay Scale: $145,000 to $170,000
 
 
Dole Packaged Foods is committed to paying our Associates fairly and equitably. The pay rate offered will consider a wide range of factors, including but not limited to experience, education, accomplishments, and location. Pay scales are subject to review on a regular basis and will be updated as appropriate.

records.title: Director of Engineering & Continuous Improvement
records.description:
**Position Summary**

The Director of Process Engineering & Continuous Improvement is the company's technical authority for how meals are made and the owner of its improvement engine. This hands-on leader combines deep manufacturing process engineering with a disciplined continuous improvement approach to make production operations more consistent, efficient, safe, and cost-effective across Mom's Meals.

The role will focus primarily on kitchen and production operations, supporting a highly automated manufacturing environment through process design, equipment performance, root cause problem solving, and structured improvement projects. The position will also support fulfillment operations by identifying automation and process opportunities that improve throughput, labor efficiency, accuracy, and customer service.

The Director partners closely with Production, Fulfillment, Supply Chain, Food Safety and Quality, Maintenance, R&D, IT, and Finance to execute strategic projects and deliver measurable, sustained improvement across the enterprise. This is a player-coach role: the Director is expected to engage directly on the production floor, lead technical problem solving, and develop the engineers and improvement practitioners on the team.

***This position will travel to our other facilities 25-50% at varying times.***

***Ideally, the selected candidate will work out of one of our Production facilities (Ankeny/Grinnell, IA, Oklahoma City, OK, or North Jackson, OH) but are open to remote for the right skills and experience.***

**Position Responsibilities may include, but not limited to**

Process & Technical Engineering

* Serve as the company's process authority for meal production, owning process design, line layouts, standard work, and process specifications for cooking, chilling, portioning, and packaging
* Lead structured process control plans, risk assessments, and capability studies to reduce variation and improve consistency
* Drive yield, discard, and portion-control improvements through engineering-based solutions
* Partner with Production, Food Safety and Quality, Maintenance and R&D teams to ensure process changes are validated, documented, and sustained on the production floor
* Reduce downtime and defects through root cause analysis and hands-on, engineering-based problem solving
* Evaluate emerging manufacturing technologies and process innovations that improve efficiency, quality, and scalability
* Ensure engineering and process solutions comply with USDA, FDA, food safety, sanitary design, and regulatory requirements

Continuous Improvement & Operational Excellence

* Build and lead a multi-site continuous improvement program, maintaining a prioritized project portfolio with defined savings targets validated with Finance
* Champion Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and structured problem-solving methodologies (such as A3, DMAIC, value stream mapping, changeover reduction, and standard work)
* Drive waste reduction, productivity improvement, and labor optimization initiatives
* Evaluate operational KPIs, including OEE, yield, labor productivity, and discards, and use data analytics to prioritize improvement opportunities
* Coach kitchen and production leaders and engineers in structured problem solving, and ensure improvements are standardized and sustained
* Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement across operations

Kitchen & Production Engineering

* Lead engineering efforts supporting highly automated meal production operations
* Drive equipment performance, uptime, and Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) improvements
* Identify ideal equipment required to produce Mom's Meals to specification at scale, including equipment that should be replaced or decommissioned and equipment that can deliver OEE improvements and a measurable return on investment
* Partner with Production leadership and Commercialization team to identify bottlenecks and improve throughput
* Lead facility expansion projects, line installations, equipment upgrades, and process redesign initiatives

Capital & Automation Projects

* Develop and manage the engineering capital plan, prioritizing projects by safety, quality, and measurable return
* Lead project prioritization, design, budgeting, vendor selection, implementation, and startup activities
* Ensure projects are completed safely, on time, and within budget
* Manage external engineering firms, contractors, equipment suppliers, and system integrators
* Build a practical, multi-year automation roadmap focused on productivity, yield, and labor efficiency
* Establish project governance, reporting, and post-implementation performance reviews

Maintenance & Reliability Partnership

* Partner with Maintenance leadership on standards for asset management, equipment lifecycle planning, and preventative, predictive, and reliability-centered maintenance practices
* Use maintenance KPIs, including downtime, PM completion rates, equipment failure rates, and maintenance costs, to prioritize engineering and improvement work

Leadership & Team Development

* Provide coaching, mentorship, and technical leadership to process engineering, continuous improvement, and engineering personnel
* Develop future engineering leaders, improvement practitioners, and technical subject matter experts
* Promote a culture focused on safety, engagement, accountability, and operational excellence

**Required Skills and Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering or related technical field
* **10+ years of progressive engineering leadership experience within manufacturing, food production, and highly automated operations, including leading process engineering or continuous improvement teams**
* Hands-on experience applying Lean and Six Sigma tools, with a demonstrated record of delivering quantified, sustained savings and performance gains
* Strong process engineering skills, including process design, root cause analysis, process capability, statistical analysis, and OEE and yield analytics
* Demonstrated success leading capital projects and automation implementations, including equipment installations and line upgrades
* Working knowledge of industrial automation, controls, packaging systems, and manufacturing technologies

records.title: Director of Process Engineering & Continuous Improvement
records.description:
The Director of Process Engineering & Continuous Improvement is the company's technical authority for how meals are made and the owner of its improvement engine. This hands-on leader combines deep manufacturing process engineering with a disciplined continuous improvement approach to make production operations more consistent, efficient, safe, and cost-effective across Mom's Meals.
 
 
The role will focus primarily on kitchen and production operations, supporting a highly automated manufacturing environment through process design, equipment performance, root cause problem solving, and structured improvement projects. The position will also support fulfillment operations by identifying automation and process opportunities that improve throughput, labor efficiency, accuracy, and customer service.
 
 
The Director partners closely with Production, Fulfillment, Supply Chain, Food Safety and Quality, Maintenance, R&D, IT, and Finance to execute strategic projects and deliver measurable, sustained improvement across the enterprise. This is a player-coach role: the Director is expected to engage directly on the production floor, lead technical problem solving, and develop the engineers and improvement practitioners on the team.
 
 
**This position will travel to our other facilities 25-50% at varying times.**
**Ideally, the selected candidate will work out of one of our Production facilities (Ankeny/Grinnell, IA, Oklahoma City, OK, or North Jackson, OH) but are open to remote for the right skills and experience.**
**Benefits**
Our employees enjoy a generous package of benefits that we are thrilled to provide, and feel is part of what makes us different as an employer. We value our team members, and this is one way we can show it.
 
 
**Benefits Include**

* PTO, holiday pay and holiday of choice
* 401(k) match
* Life insurance
* Short-term disability
* Health, dental and vision insurance
* Maternity/paternity leave
* Health savings account (HSA)
* Flex spending accounts (FSA) – health and dependent

**Position Responsibilities May Include, But Not Limited To**
Process & Technical Engineering
 
 

* Serve as the company's process authority for meal production, owning process design, line layouts, standard work, and process specifications for cooking, chilling, portioning, and packaging
* Lead structured process control plans, risk assessments, and capability studies to reduce variation and improve consistency
* Drive yield, discard, and portion-control improvements through engineering-based solutions
* Partner with Production, Food Safety and Quality, Maintenance and R&D teams to ensure process changes are validated, documented, and sustained on the production floor
* Reduce downtime and defects through root cause analysis and hands-on, engineering-based problem solving
* Evaluate emerging manufacturing technologies and process innovations that improve efficiency, quality, and scalability
* Ensure engineering and process solutions comply with USDA, FDA, food safety, sanitary design, and regulatory requirements

Continuous Improvement & Operational Excellence
 
 

* Build and lead a multi-site continuous improvement program, maintaining a prioritized project portfolio with defined savings targets validated with Finance
* Champion Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and structured problem-solving methodologies (such as A3, DMAIC, value stream mapping, changeover reduction, and standard work)
* Drive waste reduction, productivity improvement, and labor optimization initiatives
* Evaluate operational KPIs, including OEE, yield, labor productivity, and discards, and use data analytics to prioritize improvement opportunities
* Coach kitchen and production leaders and engineers in structured problem solving, and ensure improvements are standardized and sustained
* Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement across operations

Kitchen & Production Engineering
 
 

* Lead engineering efforts supporting highly automated meal production operations
* Drive equipment performance, uptime, and Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) improvements
* Identify ideal equipment required to produce Mom's Meals to specification at scale, including equipment that should be replaced or decommissioned and equipment that can deliver OEE improvements and a measurable return on investment
* Partner with Production leadership and Commercialization team to identify bottlenecks and improve throughput
* Lead facility expansion projects, line installations, equipment upgrades, and process redesign initiatives

Capital & Automation Projects
 
 

* Develop and manage the engineering capital plan, prioritizing projects by safety, quality, and measurable return
* Lead project prioritization, design, budgeting, vendor selection, implementation, and startup activities
* Ensure projects are completed safely, on time, and within budget
* Manage external engineering firms, contractors, equipment suppliers, and system integrators
* Build a practical, multi-year automation roadmap focused on productivity, yield, and labor efficiency
* Establish project governance, reporting, and post-implementation performance reviews

Maintenance & Reliability Partnership
 
 

* Partner with Maintenance leadership on standards for asset management, equipment lifecycle planning, and preventative, predictive, and reliability-centered maintenance practices
* Use maintenance KPIs, including downtime, PM completion rates, equipment failure rates, and maintenance costs, to prioritize engineering and improvement work

Leadership & Team Development
 
 

* Provide coaching, mentorship, and technical leadership to process engineering, continuous improvement, and engineering personnel
* Develop future engineering leaders, improvement practitioners, and technical subject matter experts
* Promote a culture focused on safety, engagement, accountability, and operational excellence

**Required Skills And Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering or related technical field
* 10+ years of progressive engineering leadership experience within manufacturing, food production, and highly automated operations, including leading process engineering or continuous improvement teams
* Hands-on experience applying Lean and Six Sigma tools, with a demonstrated record of delivering quantified, sustained savings and performance gains
* Strong process engineering skills, including process design, root cause analysis, process capability, statistical analysis, and OEE and yield analytics
* Demonstrated success leading capital projects and automation implementations, including equipment installations and line upgrades
* Working knowledge of industrial automation, controls, packaging systems, and manufacturing technologies
* Knowledge of Sanitary Design Principles and Standards for food manufacturing.
* Experience leading teams in regulated manufacturing environments
* Proven ability to influence cross-functional leaders and drive enterprise-wide change

**Preferred Skills And Experience**

* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification
* Food manufacturing, packaged goods, pharmaceutical, and automated distribution experience
* Experience with Industry 4.0 technologies, predictive maintenance, and digital manufacturing tools
* Experience managing and understanding facility utility controls, including HVAC, water, and steam systems
* Professional Engineer (PE) license or advanced technical degree

**Physical Requirements**

* Regularly required to use hands to feel, grab, or operate objects, tools, and controls while reaching with hands and arms
* Frequently required to stand, communicate, and listen
* Occasionally required to walk, stoop, kneel or crouch
* Occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds
* Visual perception to perform job including peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus
* Able to perform repetitive movements
* Able to work in variable temperatures (cold/hot)

**Company Overview**
Mom’s Meals is a home-delivered meal service providing fully prepared, refrigerated meal solutions direct to homes nationwide since 1999. We provide seniors, patients recovering post-discharge and those managing a chronic condition with tailored nutrition solutions to manage their specific needs. If you are passionate about the well-being of others and have a strong sense of community, Mom’s Meals could be the place for you! We are a family operated business looking for fun, compassionate, and friendly people who want to make a difference in the lives of others.
 
 
**EEO**
Mom’s Meals complies with all applicable federal and state non-discrimination laws. Qualified applicants shall receive consideration for employment without regards to race, religion, national origin, ancestry, color, gender, age, disability, or veteran status.

records.title: Division Director of Quality
records.description:
This position is incentive eligible. 
 
 

##### **Medical City Healthcare**

##### **Division Director of Quality**

##### **Full Time, Exempt**

Want to join a team of daring managers who care without reservations or limits? Our Parallon team is looking for a(an) Division Director of Quality. HCA Healthcare is an advanced healthcare network that has committed up to $300 million to our incredible team members over the course of three years.

##### **Job Summary and Qualifications**

* Provide timely consultation and support to hospital QM departments and facility and division senior management.
* Direct and coordinate QM activities of market and division teams as needed and as delegated by the DVPQ.
* Assist division facilities in strengthening proactive quality management, and performance improvement processes.
* Develop, identify, analyze, and present data for division-wide QM initiatives; guide teams in using improvement data appropriately.
* Direct the division centralized quality coordinator team, maintaining regulatory compliance with timely completion of OPPE/FPPE.
* Support facility preparation for The Joint Commission (TJC) surveys, under the direction of the Division Director of Regulatory.
* Support facility during TJC surveys and collaborate during medical staff sessions to present OPPE/FPPE data.
* Coordinate quality improvement education for hospital and medical staff when requested by senior management.
* Orient newly appointed QM directors to division and market processes.
* Represent the division at corporate meetings when requested by the DVPQ.
* Uphold the Corporate Ethics and Compliance Program, HCA Code of Conduct, and Mission and Values.

**What qualifications you will need:**

* Bachelor's degree in a healthcare-related field or comparable experience required
* Master's degree in healthcare or related field preferred
* Texas or compact Nursing license preferred.
* CPHQ preferred

##### **Benefits**

Parallon, offers a total rewards package that supports the health, life, career and retirement of our colleagues. The available plans and programs include:

* Comprehensive medical coverage that covers many common services at no cost or for a low copay. Plans include prescription drug and behavioral health coverage as well as free telemedicine services and free AirMed medical transportation.
* Additional options for dental and vision benefits, life and disability coverage, flexible spending accounts, supplemental health protection plans (accident, critical illness, hospital indemnity), auto and home insurance, identity theft protection, legal counseling, long-term care coverage, moving assistance, pet insurance and more.
* Free counseling services and resources for emotional, physical and financial wellbeing
* 401(k) Plan with a 100% match on 3% to 9% of pay (based on years of service)
* Employee Stock Purchase Plan with 10% off HCA Healthcare stock
* Family support through fertility and family building benefits with Progyny and adoption assistance.
* Referral services for child, elder and pet care, home and auto repair, event planning and more
* Consumer discounts through Abenity and Consumer Discounts
* Retirement readiness, rollover assistance services and preferred banking partnerships
* Education assistance (tuition, student loan, certification support, dependent scholarships)
* Colleague recognition program
* Time Away From Work Program (paid time off, paid family leave, long- and short-term disability coverage and leaves of absence)
* Employee Health Assistance Fund that offers free employee-only coverage to full-time and part-time colleagues based on income.

Learn more about Employee Benefits

***Note: Eligibility for benefits may vary by location.***

HCA Healthcare is committed to research and clinical protocols. Do you want to impact standards of care and save lives across the country? Apply today to our Division Director of Quality and be a part of the innovation of ideas.

Medical City Healthcare strives to deliver excellence. We are committed to the care and improvement of human life. We provide the highest quality, cost-effective healthcare in the communities we serve. Medical City Healthcare is one of the North Texas region’s largest and most comprehensive healthcare providers. We have 16 hospitals, 5,000 physicians and more than 17,000 employees in Dallas-Fort Worth. Medical City Healthcare is the only healthcare system in North Texas with an adult and children’s hospital on the same campus. We are a part of HCA Healthcare. HCA Healthcare includes 185 hospitals in the United States and England. Medical City Healthcare has six hospitals that are Magnet® recognized by the American Nurses Credentialing Center Magnet Recognition Program®. We have been recognized by Texas Monthly as a Best Companies to Work for in Texas. HCA Healthcare has been named to LinkedIn’s 2021 Top Companies list of 50 best workplaces to grow your career.

HCA Healthcare has been recognized as one of the World’s Most Ethical Companies® by the Ethisphere Institute more than ten times. In recent years, HCA Healthcare spent an estimated $3.7 billion in cost for the delivery of charitable care, uninsured discounts, and other uncompensated expenses.

Â

"Good people beget good people."- Dr. Thomas Frist, Sr. 
HCA Healthcare Co-Founder

Unlock your potential with a leading healthcare provider dedicated to its patients, colleagues and communities. Help guide our team as a(an) Division Director of Quality and **help us improve more lives in more ways**.

*We are an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.*

records.title: Corporate Director of Quality
records.description:
Take the next step with an exciting and growing company
 
As the only fully integrated maker of premium quality wire, rope, and assemblies, Loos & Co holds a leading position in the global aerospace sector.
 
A division of the Central Wire (CWI) Group of Companies encompassing 12 locations in three countries, 750+ employees, and over six decades of excellence, Loos & Co solutions are found in mission critical flight control applications. Our precision-manufactured components are also used for defense, med tech, and heavy industry purposes around the world, in large part because of the people behind our products.
 
Do you have a strong work ethic? Take pride in a job well done? Are you passionate about contributing to individual and team, company and customer successes? If you’re interested in joining a dynamic work environment that offers opportunities to reach your full potential, we want to hear from you.
 
 
Position Summary / Essential Function
 
The Corporate Director of Quality is CWI’s senior enterprise Quality leader and is responsible for establishing and sustaining a culture of quality excellence, accountability, customer focus, product safety, and continuous improvement across aerospace, commercial, medical, metal rope, and assembly facilities. Based in Pomfret Center, Connecticut and reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the Director leads the enterprise Quality function, develops high-performing teams of Quality professionals, and establishes the governance, systems, standards, metrics, and decision rights required for consistent execution across all locations.
 
A central responsibility of the role is to create a results- and data-driven culture in which decisions are based on objective evidence, process capability, customer and regulatory requirements, risk, and measurable business outcomes. The Director advances the organization from reactive inspection and problem resolution toward prevention, disciplined problem solving, statistical thinking, robust corrective action, and sustained operational excellence.
 
The Director maintains the effectiveness and certification readiness of applicable quality management systems, including AS9100D and ISO 9001 for aviation, space, defense, and commercial operations; ISO 13485 for medical-device operations where applicable; and customer-, product-, and facility-specific requirements for metal rope, wire rope, cable, and assemblies. The role ensures that customer and applicable statutory and regulatory requirements take precedence where they exceed or conflict with general quality-system requirements.
 
Key Responsibilities
 

* Build, lead, develop, and retain a high-performing organization of Quality professionals across CWI, with clear roles, decision rights, measurable objectives, development plans, succession pipelines, and performance expectations.
* Create a results- and data-driven culture of Quality excellence in which teams use objective evidence, trend analysis, statistical methods, and risk-based thinking to identify priorities, prevent defects, and verify sustained improvement.
* Establish and execute the enterprise Quality strategy, organizational design, staffing plan, technical roadmap, and resource priorities in alignment with CWI business and operating objectives.
* Own enterprise governance for quality management systems and maintain certification readiness for applicable aerospace, commercial, medical, metal rope, and assembly facilities, including registrar, customer, regulatory, and internal audits.
* Ensure aerospace quality controls address AS9100D requirements, including operational risk management, configuration management, product safety, counterfeit-parts prevention, special-process control, production process verification, foreign-object damage prevention, traceability, and awareness of ethical behavior.
* Ensure first article inspection and production process verification practices align with AS9102 when contractually applicable, and ensure special processes are qualified, controlled, and approved to customer, regulatory, or other requirements where applicable.
* Ensure medical quality-system controls align with ISO 13485 and applicable regulatory and customer requirements, including risk management, validated processes, traceability, complaint handling, CAPA, change control, and record retention.
* Establish common standards for document and record control, calibration, inspection and test, nonconforming output, CAPA, root-cause analysis, internal auditing, management review, supplier quality, customer complaints, product and process change control, and continuous improvement.
* Establish an enterprise Quality performance-management system with leading and lagging indicators for customer complaints, escapes, first-pass yield, scrap and rework, cost of poor quality, supplier defects, audit findings, process capability, CAPA aging, recurrence, and corrective-action effectiveness.
* Lead monthly operating reviews and formal management reviews that convert Quality data into executive-level insights, identify systemic and emerging risks, assign accountable owners, and track actions through verified closure.
* Develop Quality leaders who can influence Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Commercial teams; make risk-based decisions; escalate product-safety or conformity concerns; and hold the organization accountable for results.
* Serve as the senior Quality escalation point for significant customer complaints, product escapes, product-safety events, audit findings, systemic nonconformances, supplier-quality issues, and certification or regulatory risks.
* Ensure robust containment, root-cause analysis, corrective action, effectiveness verification, and lessons-learned deployment for significant or recurring failures, including consideration of human factors where relevant.
* Provide enterprise oversight for supplier-quality strategy, supplier qualification, risk-based surveillance, source inspection, flow-down of customer and regulatory requirements, and supplier corrective action.
* Partner with the Chief Operating Officer, Plant Managers, Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Commercial, and other leaders to integrate Quality into operational performance, new-product introduction, manufacturing transfers, and change management.
* Communicate Quality-system health, certification status, customer performance, material risks, resource needs, and improvement results clearly to executive leadership and the Board or ownership group when requested.
* Perform other related duties consistent with the role, grade, and business needs.

Required Qualifications
 

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Materials Science, Metallurgy, Quality, Manufacturing, or a closely related technical discipline.
* Twelve or more years of progressive Quality, manufacturing, engineering, or operational leadership experience in regulated or high-reliability manufacturing.
* At least seven years of direct people-leadership experience, including leadership of Quality managers and professionals, performance management, coaching, organizational design, and succession planning.
* At least five years of multi-site or enterprise Quality leadership experience with accountability for common systems, audits, metrics, and cross-site standardization.
* Demonstrated responsibility for an AS9100D-certified quality management system and successful participation as the senior Quality leader in at least one third-party certification or recertification cycle.
* Demonstrated experience with internal and external audit programs, management review, CAPA, root-cause analysis, configuration and change control, supplier quality, product safety, traceability, nonconformance control, and customer complaint resolution.
* Demonstrated use of Quality data and statistical methods to improve performance, including examples of measurable reduction in defects, escapes, cost of poor quality, or recurring corrective actions.
* Ability to travel approximately 25% to 40% to CWI facilities, customer sites, supplier sites, and audit locations, with additional travel during significant launches, audits, or quality events.
* Ability to communicate technical and business risk, priorities, decisions, and performance clearly to plant, functional, customer, registrar, and executive audiences.

Preferred Qualifications
 

* Experience in specialty metals, wire, cable, wire rope, aircraft cable, mechanical cable, swaging, metal assemblies, or other highly engineered metal products.
* Experience leading Quality in aerospace and defense manufacturing, including customer flow-downs, AS9102 first article inspection, source inspection, special processes, counterfeit-parts controls, configuration management, product safety, and foreign-object damage prevention.
* Experience with ISO 13485-certified medical-device manufacturing and risk-management practices aligned with ISO 14971 where applicable.
* Experience with Nadcap-accredited special processes, Defense Contract Management Agency oversight, Federal Aviation Administration-regulated products, or major aerospace prime and Tier 1 customer requirements, as applicable to CWI’s business.
* Advanced degree in Engineering, Operations, Quality, or Business Administration.
* Experience using an electronic QMS, ERP, business-intelligence, and statistical software to manage Quality performance and traceability.

Preferred Certifications
 

* ASQ Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE) or equivalent senior Quality leadership credential.
* ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), ASQ Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), or AS9100 Lead Auditor certification.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or Master Black Belt.
* Certified Manufacturing Engineer, Professional Engineer, Project Management Professional, or comparable technical credential as relevant.

Key Leadership Competencies
 

* Enterprise Quality leadership and culture building
* Leadership, development, and retention of Quality professionals
* Results orientation and measurable accountability
* Data-driven decision making and statistical thinking
* AS9100D, ISO 9001, and regulated quality-system leadership
* Product safety, compliance, and risk-based judgment
* CAPA, root-cause analysis, and corrective-action effectiveness
* Customer quality and executive escalation
* Cross-functional influence and change leadership
* Continuous improvement and operational excellence
* Executive communication and management review
* Multi-site governance and standardization

Leadership Standard
 
Success in this position is measured not simply by maintaining certifications or passing audits, but by the Director’s ability to build capable Quality leaders and teams, establish measurable accountability, improve the effectiveness of CWI’s quality systems, reduce recurring failures and customer escapes, strengthen process capability, protect product safety and conformity, and demonstrate sustained improvement through objective performance data.
 
Physical and Work Environment Requirements
 
The role operates in office and active manufacturing environments and requires regular interaction with plant operations. It may require walking or standing on production floors, observing machinery and manufacturing activities, using a computer and quality information systems, and communicating in areas where hearing protection or other personal protective equipment is required. Travel among company locations, customer sites, supplier sites, and audit locations is expected. Reasonable accommodations will be considered in accordance with applicable law. This description identifies the essential functions of the position but is not intended to list every physical activity or working condition.
 
Base Salary Range
 
$142,000-$204,500
 
Benefits
 
Subject to the terms, eligibility requirements, and amendment provisions of the applicable plans and policies:
 

* 401(k) with matching
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Referral program
* Tuition reimbursement
* Vision insurance

Pre-Employment Drug Testing
 
All applicants who are offered a position with the Company will be required to successfully complete a post-offer drug screening, where permitted by applicable law and in accordance with Company policy.
 
At-Will Employment
 
Employment with the Company is at will. Either the employee or the Company may terminate employment at any time, with or without cause or notice, subject to applicable law. Nothing in this job description creates a contract of employment or alters the at-will employment relationship.
 
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
 
The Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer and prohibits discrimination or harassment based on any protected characteristic under federal, state, or local law.
 
 
**Benefits:** 

* Health, Dental and Vision insurance options
* Life insurance
* 401(k) with company match
* Paid time off
* Employee assistance program
* Employee Referral program
* Tuition reimbursement

**Shift:** 8-hour shift
 
**Work Location:** In person, Company does not provide relocation assistance.
 
Central Wire Group of Companies is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability status, or any other applicable characteristics protected by law.
 
Central Wire Group of Companies is a Drug-free workplace and pre-employment drug tests and background checks are required.

records.title: Director of Quality Assurance & CI
records.description:
**Lead the Transformation. Build a Culture of Excellence. Deliver Results That Last.**

The Director of Quality Assurance & Continuous Improvement provides strategic leadership for the company's quality and continuous improvement functions, ensuring products, processes, and services consistently meet the highest standards of quality, reliability, and customer satisfaction. This role is responsible for developing, implementing, and continuously improving the Quality Management System (QMS) while driving a culture of operational excellence across the organization. Leading enterprise-wide Lean initiatives, Kaizen events, root cause analysis, and structured continuous improvement programs, this position delivers measurable improvements in quality, productivity, cost, and operational performance. Working closely with executive leadership and cross-functional teams, the Director establishes quality strategies, drives compliance with customer and regulatory requirements, and champions sustainable improvements that support the company's strategic growth objectives.

**What Success looks Like**

* Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the company's Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring compliance with customer, regulatory, and industry standards, including ISO certifications.
* Establish enterprise-wide quality strategies, policies, and governance while serving as the executive leader for quality-related decisions impacting customers, operations, and suppliers.
* Drive a culture of operational excellence by leading Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, and structured continuous improvement initiatives across all business functions.
* Develop and execute strategic cost reduction initiatives that improve productivity, eliminate waste, reduce the Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ), and enhance overall operational performance.
* Partner cross-functionally with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Finance, Sales, and executive leadership to identify, prioritize, and deliver sustainable business improvements.
* Champion the voice of the customer by leveraging customer feedback, warranty data, and field performance to improve product quality, reliability, and customer satisfaction.
* Lead enterprise-wide root cause analysis and corrective action processes to resolve quality issues, prevent recurrence, and strengthen operational performance.
* Oversee internal and external audit programs, ensuring compliance with quality, safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements while proactively managing organizational risk.
* Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing Quality and Continuous Improvement organization while coaching leaders throughout the business to embed a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
* Establish, monitor, and report key performance indicators (KPIs) that measure quality, delivery, cost savings, productivity, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement performance.
* Translate strategic business objectives into measurable quality and operational improvement initiatives that deliver sustainable financial and operational results.
* Build trusted relationships across the organization and with external stakeholders, influencing decision-making and driving alignment to achieve the company's strategic objectives.

**Qualifications That Shine**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field required; Master's degree or other advanced degree preferred.
* 15+ years of progressive quality leadership experience, including 10+ years leading people and 5+ years leading corporate or multi-site quality organizations.
* Proven success developing and leading Quality Management Systems (QMS) within a manufacturing environment, including ISO implementation, certification, and ongoing compliance.
* Professional certifications such as ASQ Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt, and Lean certification are strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated success leading Lean transformation, Kaizen events, and enterprise-wide continuous improvement initiatives that deliver measurable business results.
* Strong knowledge of quality systems, root cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions (CAPA), statistical process control (SPC), and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Proven ability to influence executive leadership and build collaborative partnerships across operations, engineering, supply chain, finance, and commercial teams.
* Exceptional communication, presentation, and organizational skills with the ability to translate strategy into execution and drive organizational change.
* Strategic, data-driven leader with a track record of improving quality, operational performance, customer satisfaction, and financial results through operational excellence initiatives.

**Why You’ll Love Working Here**

* **You’ll Be Empowered** **–** You’ll have autonomy in your role, supported by a team that trusts your judgment
* **You’ll Grow With Us** **–** We invest in your training, development, and long-term career path
* **You’ll Be Rewarded** **–** Competitive pay, performance incentives, 401(k) with profit sharing, and great benefits
* **You’ll Make a Real Impact** **–** Your work supports businesses across North America and shapes the future of finishing technology
* **You’ll Join a Great Team** **–** We’re growing fast, we value collaboration, and are committed to your success

**Transparent Rewards** 
 
At GFS, we recognize the dedication behind every role and ensure that our compensation reflects both your impact and our shared success.

**Pay Range:** $124,518 – $156,746 per year, based on your experience, skills, and qualifications.

**Bonus Eligibility:** This position is eligible for an annual individual incentive based on company performance. Maximum bonus amounts may vary depending on role.

**Benefits:** Eligible for standard company benefits, including health, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) retirement plan with company match, paid time off, and other employee programs. More detailed information is available at 2026 GFS Benefits.

Actual compensation will be determined by factors including experience, education, certifications, skill level, and market conditions. For remote or hybrid positions, the listed pay range applies to applicants in the specified location.

**About GFS**

Global Finishing Solutions is the leading manufacturer of paint booths and finishing systems serving automotive, aerospace, industrial manufacturing, marine, military, rail, trucking, and wood finishing markets. We specialize in building custom solutions that meet each customer’s unique needs—and we do it with a team that thrives on collaboration and innovation because we're different.

What makes us different is our unwavering commitment to our core values of family, respect, partnership, improvement, and integrity. We are a family-oriented organization that still values the little things, creating a workplace where you can thrive, fairness guides every decision, and collaboration drives shared success. Small town in spirit but big-hearted in impact, here you’re not just joining a company—you’re joining a team that grows together, celebrates together, and builds lasting value together. That’s the difference. Join us.

Apply now at www.gfscareers.us

About GFS 
Watch Us in Action 
Connect on LinkedIn

**Equal Opportunity Employer**

***GFS is proud to provide equal employment opportunities to all applicants***. We welcome candidates of all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, sex, age, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, or any other status protected by law. Employment offers are subject to successful completion of pre-employment drug screening and physicals, consistent with applicable laws.

*Note to recruiters: GFS only works with agencies that have signed a contract with our HR team. Resumes sent directly to hiring managers without a prior agreement are considered unsolicited and the property of GFS. Placement fees will not be paid without a formal contract.*

records.title: Director, Quality
records.description:
**Position Summary**
--------------------

The Director, Quality is responsible for leading multiple manufacturing/service sites and/or corporate quality resources in the execution of the overall STERIS Quality System. This position is principally responsible for manufacturing/service site or functional quality system execution to drive product/service quality improvement and ensure compliance with, as appropriate, ISO 9001, ISO 13485, MDSAP, FDA QMSR CFR Part 820/211, EU MDR, and other applicable standards. Supporting the GI Reprocessing business, this role provides quality leadership for products, processes, and services that help healthcare providers safely clean, disinfect, and reprocess gastrointestinal endoscopes and related equipment. The Director will champion a culture of quality, compliance, and continuous improvement, helping ensure the delivery of safe, effective, and reliable solutions that support infection prevention, patient safety, and customer confidence. The Quality Director will lead teams of quality managers and engineers responsible for product and service quality, supplier quality, new product/service support, continuous improvement initiatives, and quality system execution. This leader will partner closely with Operations, Engineering, Regulatory Affairs, and Commercial teams to drive operational excellence, mitigate risk, support innovation, and enhance quality performance across the GI Reprocessing portfolio.

Preferred onsite location: Mentor, OH, with consideration for candidates based in Plymouth, MN or Conroe, TX.

**What You’ll do as a Director Quality**
----------------------------------------

* The Director, Quality will have responsibility for the following: Leads manufacturing/service sites and/or corporate quality staff in the execution and continuous improvement of the STERIS Quality System. Operates with a focus on the following objectives:
 + Ensures site level compliance to appropriate ISO, FDA, and other applicable regulatory standards.
 + Drives strategies and methods to continuously improve capital, consumable and service product quality performance.
 + Establishes clear and consistent quality measurement systems in order to monitor and drive results.
 + Leads quality planning and the execution of assigned New Product/Service Development (NPD) projects to achieve targeted quality deliverable adherence.
 + Drives targeted supplier quality improvement efforts and oversees supplier evaluation, approval, and control for assigned manufacturing sites.
 + Assists in the continuous improvement and standardization of quality system procedures and monitor effectiveness.
 + Supports the reliability function by integrating design for reliability tools and techniques within the local projects.
 + Leads quality planning efforts through cross-functional teaming at a site level.
* Supports the New Product/Service Development process and projects to ensure projects attain cost, quality, and delivery objectives.
* Directs local staff on planning sequential and concurrent quality activities. Establish planning and monitoring tools and techniques.
* Provides Quality viewpoints and opinions in planning and specifying existing and future products.
* Assists in the development of the Quality budget. Helps to ensures resources are adequate to fully support the Quality System.
* Takes ownership of all local quality issues, projects, and development activities. Works closely with the site’s Senior Management Teams to provide strategic direction and development of the manufacturing sites product quality strategies and tactics.
* Manages and provide direction to a teams of quality professionals both at corporate and manufacturing sites, with responsibility for hiring, performance management, appropriate staffing, and deployment of resources.
* Assures that local sites maintain and improve operational and quality systems to remain in a state of compliance to appropriate ISO, FDA, and other applicable regulatory standards.
* Works closely with the regulatory function to ensure compliance to appropriate ISO and FDA standards; plans for and assists in the management of external audits.

records.description:
**Job Description:**

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Head of Global Quality Strategic Initiatives is responsible for defining, leading and executing enterprise-wide initiatives that strengthen TransMedics’ global quality management system (QMS), enhance regulatory compliance, improve product quality and patient safety, and advance operational excellence across the product lifecycle.

Partnering closely with executive leadership and cross-functional teams, this leader translates business priorities into measurable quality outcomes. The role drives complex transformation programs, anticipates emerging quality and regulatory risks, and establishes the processes, governance and metrics needed to support growth while maintaining high standards of safety, effectiveness and compliance.

The successful candidate combines deep medical device quality and regulatory expertise with strategic vision, strong business acumen and exceptional program leadership, with the ability to influence at every level of a global organization.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

This position is responsible for, but not limited to, the following:

* Develop and execute a multi-year global quality roadmap aligned with business priorities, regulatory expectations and patient safety. Identify systemic issues and emerging risks, prioritize transformation initiatives, and integrate quality priorities into business planning, product development and growth.
* Lead a portfolio of cross-functional quality programs with clear scope, milestones, resources, accountability and measurable outcomes. Establish executive steering committees, decision rights and escalation paths; resolve barriers, recommend investment priorities and track business impact and sustained results.
* Improve and harmonize the global QMS in line with FDA QMSR (21 CFR Part 820), ISO 13485, EU MDR and other applicable requirements. Strengthen process ownership, management review and effectiveness monitoring while accommodating regional requirements and local operating needs.
* Oversee improvement programs spanning document and records management, design and manufacturing controls, risk management, supplier quality, nonconformance, corrective and preventive action (CAPA), change control and post-market processes.
* Partner with Regulatory Affairs and site Quality leaders to assess regulatory changes and lead enterprise remediation programs addressing audit findings, regulatory observations and emerging risks. Support FDA inspections and external audits, resolve root causes, and embed sustainable inspection readiness.
* Define enterprise quality KPIs and key risk indicators covering CAPA effectiveness, complaints, nonconformances, audit findings, suppliers and product quality. Build consistent dashboards and executive reporting that improve visibility into risks, trends and program progress.
* Sponsor electronic QMS, quality data integration, advanced analytics and appropriate AI-enabled initiatives within applicable validation, privacy, security and regulatory controls. Promote data integrity, traceability and evidence-based decisions.
* Partner with functional leaders to strengthen product risk management, complaint handling, adverse event reporting, field action assessment and post-market monitoring from development and design transfer through manufacturing and post-market surveillance. Lead analysis of recurring issues and systemic failure modes to improve detection, containment and prevention.
* Apply Lean, Six Sigma and risk-based problem-solving to reduce rework, scrap, variation and the cost of poor quality while protecting compliance and patient safety. Partner with Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply Chain and site leaders to improve process capability and supplier performance, replicate best practices and measure benefits.
* Advise the Chief Regulatory Officer and executive leadership on quality priorities, systemic risks and transformation opportunities; communicate with the Board as appropriate. Influence priorities and resource decisions, mentor quality and program leaders, and lead training and change management that build accountability, transparency and lasting quality ownership.
* Collaborate with IT/Digital, Finance, Human Resources and other internal partners, and engage regulatory authorities, notified and certification bodies, external auditors, strategic suppliers, consultants and industry organizations as needed.
* Success will be measured by on-time transformation milestones; stronger QMS effectiveness and consistency; fewer recurring issues, overdue corrective actions and repeat audit findings; sustained inspection readiness; and measurable improvements in product quality, complaint trends, supplier performance and cost of poor quality.
* Perform other TransMedics tasks and duties as assigned.

**MANAGEMENT RESPONSIBILITIES**

Convene and lead cross-functional teams, establish program governance, and develop and mentor quality and program leaders within the approved mandate, budget and governance structure. Direct-report responsibilities are to be confirmed. Formal authority for regulatory decisions, product disposition, quality approvals and regulatory reporting remains with the accountable functions under company procedures.

**PHYSICAL ATTRIBUTES**

This is an on-site role in Andover or Somerville, MA, with approximately 10–20% travel. Additional essential physical requirements, if applicable, are to be confirmed.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

 

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Life Sciences, Quality, Regulatory Affairs or a related technical discipline.
* 15+ years of progressive experience in medical devices, combination products or another highly regulated healthcare industry, including significant leadership experience in Quality, Regulatory Affairs, quality transformation or enterprise program management.
* Proven success leading complex quality improvement, remediation or organizational change programs across business units, manufacturing sites and geographies, translating strategy into executable plans and measurable, sustainable results.
* Strong knowledge of FDA medical device requirements, including QMSR, and working knowledge of ISO 13485, ISO 14971, EU MDR and applicable global medical device frameworks.
* Hands-on experience with CAPA, nonconformances, complaints, design controls, supplier quality, change management, audits, remediation and post-market surveillance; understanding of root cause analysis, process validation, manufacturing controls and QMS effectiveness.
* Familiarity with electronic QMS platforms, quality data analytics and computerized system validation or assurance (CSV/CSA) principles.
* Ability to influence senior executives and stakeholders in a global matrix organization, communicate complex issues clearly, and drive decisions without relying on direct authority.
* Demonstrated strategic thinking, analytical problem-solving, change leadership and talent development, with sound risk-based judgment, integrity and accountability for product quality, patient safety and regulatory compliance.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

 

* Advanced degree in Engineering, Life Sciences, Business Administration or a related field.
* Professional certifications in quality (ASQ CQE or CMQ/OE), regulatory affairs (RAC), program management (PMP), Lean Six Sigma or change management.
* Experience with MasterControl.

As part of our long-term growth plans, TransMedics is excited to announce our plan to relocate our headquarters (HQ) to Somerville, MA by 2028. We chose this location because we believe it is a place where innovation will thrive. Our new state-of-the-art headquarters is designed to support collaboration, creativity, and discovery. We believe this will be a place where we can continue to do things few thought possible in organ transplantation to help patients. *Specific timing and role impact may vary.*

TransMedics, Inc. is a commercial-stage medical technology company transforming organ transplant therapy for patients worldwide. Our mission is to help save more patients’ lives by increasing access to viable donor organs for those who are awaiting an organ transplant. To accomplish this mission, we partner closely with transplant stakeholders worldwide and help expand their access to healthy donor organs, while delivering the highest quality technology, service, clinical care and outcomes. 
 
Driven by a passion for improving patient care, we make the impossible possible and keep our employees at the center of everything we do. Together, we strive to enhance the quality of life for transplant recipients and their families, fostering hope and healing in the journey toward better health. 
 
**Maximize your potential at TransMedics, Inc.** 
www.TransMedics.com

TransMedics is committed to equitable and transparent compensation. The expected base salary range for this role is $232,800-$331,350, which represents the company’s current good-faith estimate of compensation for this position. Actual salary will depend on factors such as, but not limited to, candidate experience, qualifications, skills, and the specific work location. This role may also be eligible for bonuses, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package (medical, dental, vision, retirement savings, paid time off, and wellness resources). We comply with all U.S. pay transparency laws and do not request or consider salary history.

**Employee Benefit:**

Medical with Health Reimbursement Account through Blue Cross/Blue Shield of MA

Dental

Vision

Healthcare Flexible Spending Account

Dependent Care Flexible Spending Account

Short Term Disability

Long Term Disability

401K Plan

Pet insurance

Employee Stock Purchase Plan

TransMedics is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, marital status, age, disability or protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

records.title: Sr. Director of Quality
records.description:
The Senior Director of Quality is responsible for leading quality, regulatory compliance, and functions at an assigned facility while providing strategic leadership, guidance, and support to Quality departments across multiple FCAH locations and operating companies. This role ensures compliance with applicable FAA, EASA, customer, and industry requirements while driving consistency in quality standards, processes, audit readiness, corrective actions, and continuous improvement throughout the organization.

The Senior Director serves as a hands-on quality leader at their assigned location while partnering with site leadership and other Quality leaders to strengthen quality systems, address regulatory and operational risks, develop quality teams, and promote a culture of accountability, safety, and excellence across the organization.

**Essential Job Functions:**

**Site Quality Leadership**

* Lead and manage the Quality department at the assigned facility, ensuring compliance with applicable regulatory, customer, and company requirements.
* Partner with site leadership, Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Supply Chain, and other departments to integrate quality into daily operations and decision-making.
* Oversee site quality personnel, including staffing, performance management, training, development, and accountability.
* Ensure the facility maintains required certifications, approvals, manuals, procedures, and quality systems.
* Monitor site quality performance, identify areas of risk, and develop action plans to address deficiencies and improve operational performance.

**Multi-Site Quality Leadership & Support**

* Provide leadership, guidance, and support to Quality departments and leaders across other First Class Air operating companies and locations.
* Partner with site Quality leaders to identify challenges, strengthen quality processes, and improve regulatory compliance and operational effectiveness.
* Promote consistency in quality standards, processes, procedures, and best practices across locations where appropriate.
* Assist other locations with quality initiatives, regulatory concerns, audit preparation, corrective actions, customer issues, and process improvement efforts.
* Conduct site visits to evaluate quality systems, identify opportunities for improvement, and provide support to local Quality teams.
* Share lessons learned, recurring quality issues, and best practices across locations to prevent repeat findings and improve overall organizational performance.
* Help develop and implement company-wide quality initiatives while allowing for site-specific requirements, certifications, and regulatory differences.
* Escalate significant regulatory, operational, customer, or quality risks to executive leadership.

**Regulatory Compliance & Oversight**

* Ensure compliance with applicable FAA, EASA, UK CAA, , customer, and other regulatory requirements, as applicable to company operations.
* Maintain strong working knowledge of FAA regulations, including Part 145, Part 43, and Part 21, as applicable.
* Serve as a point of contact for regulatory authorities, customer representatives, and external auditors, as appropriate.
* Monitor regulatory changes and ensure applicable requirements are communicated and implemented across affected locations.
* Ensure maintenance, repair, overhaul, inspection, manufacturing, and other applicable activities are performed in accordance with approved technical data, regulatory requirements, and established procedures.
* Maintain organizational readiness for regulatory, customer, and third-party audits.

**Quality Management Systems**

* Develop, implement, maintain, and continuously improve Quality Management Systems (QMS) at the assigned location and across other locations as needed.
* Establish and promote consistent quality standards, policies, procedures, and best practices across the organization.
* Oversee the development, revision, and implementation of quality manuals, procedures, inspection programs, and supporting documentation.
* Ensure appropriate document control, records management, inspection processes, calibration programs, personnel qualifications, training, and other critical quality system controls are maintained.
* Partner with site and enterprise leadership to improve quality processes, reduce risk, and enhance operational performance.

**Audits, Corrective Actions & Continuous Improvement**

* Lead and oversee internal, external, regulatory, customer, and third-party audits at the assigned facility.
* Support and provide guidance to other locations in preparation for and execution of audits.
* Develop and support risk-based audit schedules and audit strategies.
* Ensure audit findings and quality issues are appropriately investigated, contained, corrected, and documented.
* Oversee corrective and preventive action (CAPA) processes and ensure root cause analysis is appropriately performed.
* Verify corrective actions are effective and prevent recurring issues.
* Identify recurring findings, systemic quality issues, and trends across locations and implement improvements where appropriate.

**Airworthiness & Technical Quality**

* Provide oversight of airworthiness and return-to-service processes across applicable repair station operations.
* Ensure appropriate controls are maintained for FAA Form 8130-3, EASA Form 1, inspection, certification, and related airworthiness documentation, as applicable.
* Ensure receiving, in-process, and final inspections are performed in accordance with applicable procedures and requirements.
* Oversee the management and control of capability lists, personnel authorizations, technician and inspector qualifications, stamps, and related records.
* Ensure calibration programs and control of tools, equipment, and test instruments meet applicable requirements.
* Assist other locations with technical quality concerns, inspection processes, airworthiness issues, and regulatory interpretations as needed.

**Customer & Supplier Quality**

* Provide leadership and support in resolving significant customer quality concerns, escalations, and recurring issues.
* Partner with Sales, Operations, Maintenance, and other departments to ensure customer quality expectations are understood and met.
* Monitor supplier-related quality trends and recurring issues.
* Support supplier corrective actions, quality investigations, and improvement initiatives as needed.
* Serve as a quality escalation resource for customer and supplier issues across locations.

**Quality Performance, Reporting & Risk Management**

* Establish and monitor quality performance metrics, KPIs, trends, and reporting processes for the assigned facility.
* Support the development and implementation of company-wide quality dashboards and performance metrics.
* Evaluate quality data to identify trends, recurring issues, risks, and opportunities for improvement.
* Communicate significant quality concerns, regulatory risks, audit findings, and improvement initiatives to site leadership and executive leadership.
* Partner with leadership to prioritize quality initiatives and allocate resources appropriately.
* Provide visibility into quality performance across locations and recommend actions to improve overall company performance.

**Requirements:**

* Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in aviation, aerospace, MRO, manufacturing, or another highly regulated environment.
* Minimum of 7 years of progressive leadership experience in Quality, Regulatory Compliance,, Inspection, or related functions preferred.
* Significant experience leading Quality functions within aviation maintenance, repair, overhaul, manufacturing, or FAA-certified repair station environments.
* Experience supporting multiple departments, facilities, locations, or business units.
* Experience working directly with FAA, EASA, UK CAA, customer representatives, or other regulatory authorities preferred.
* Demonstrated experience leading regulatory, customer, internal, and external audits.
* Experience developing, implementing, and maintaining Quality Management Systems.
* Strong working knowledge of FAA regulations, particularly Part 145, Part 43, and Part 21, as applicable.
* Knowledge of EASA, UK CAA,, and other applicable regulatory requirements preferred.
* Strong understanding of Quality Management Systems (QMS), corrective and preventive action (CAPA), root cause analysis, risk management, audit processes, and continuous improvement.
* Ability to interpret technical data, regulatory requirements, manuals, procedures, engineering documentation, and quality standards.
* This role will require 20%-30% travel to other facilities

records.title: Director, Quality Operations
records.description:
**Revvity**

Revvity is a developer and provider of end-to-end solutions designed to help scientists, researchers, and clinicians solve the world’s greatest health challenges. We pair the enthusiasm of an industry disruptor with the experience of a longtime leader. Our team of 11,000+ colleagues from around the globe are vital to our success and the reason we’re able to push boundaries in pursuit of better human health.

Find your future at Revvity.

Our team is seeking a Director, Quality Operations to lead site quality for the Hopkinton-based operation. This role succeeds the current site quality leadership position and is intentionally scoped at the Director level because it combines broad operational accountability, organizational build-out, and a significant quality-system integration mandate. The Director will lead a blended Quality Operations organization spanning product quality, quality systems, supplier and incoming quality, inspection, and production support. The successful leader must protect ongoing product quality and compliance while progressively simplifying, integrating, and modernizing the operating model.

 
 

**Routine Responsibilities:**
-----------------------------

**Site Quality Leadership and Governance**
------------------------------------------

* Quality Operations leader for Hopkinton, with accountability for product quality, manufacturing quality, inspection, release, and site QMS execution.

* Provide visible, hands-on leadership in production and laboratory environments, enabling rapid risk-based decisions and timely escalation of material, process, product, and compliance issues.

* Own the site quality operating rhythm, including management review, quality metrics, risk review, resource prioritization, and cross-functional governance with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, R&D, Regulatory, Service, and Commercial teams.

* Serve as the principal site Quality representative for FDA, ISO, notified-body, customer, and internal audits, and ensure sustained inspection readiness across the blended operation.

* Balance product continuity, customer commitments, compliance, and transformation priorities using documented risk-based decisions.

 
 

**QMS, SOP, and Digital-System Integration**
--------------------------------------------

* Create and execute a phased roadmap improve and sustain SOPs and QMS structures supporting the site, with clear process ownership, sequencing, change controls, validation needs, and business-continuity safeguards.

* Optimize operating model for document control, production records, training, calibration, internal audits, supplier management, incoming inspection, final acceptance, complaints, and customer field interfaces.

* Lead the integration and modernization of quality tools and records currently distributed across systems and methods.

* Partner with enterprise Quality, Regulatory, IT/Digital, and business process owners to deploy scalable solutions and eliminate duplicate or conflicting workflows, records, and controls.

* Ensure data integrity, validated-state control, traceability, retention, access, and training are maintained throughout system and process transitions.

 
 

**Product and Manufacturing Quality**
-------------------------------------

* Lead quality support for a diverse portfolio that includes instruments, consumables and reagents platforms.

* Oversee incoming inspection, in-process controls, final product acceptance and release, nonconformance and material-review processes, manufacturing investigations, and CAPA effectiveness.

* Ensure appropriate validation and verification of manufacturing processes, equipment, software-enabled tools, inspection methods, and test methods.

* Drive preventive product-quality improvements using defect, yield, scrap, complaint, service, supplier, and Cost of Poor Quality trends.

* Represent Quality in design transfer, manufacturing transfer, new-product introduction, supplier changes, capacity expansion, and sustaining-engineering decisions.

 
 

**Organization Build and People Leadership**
--------------------------------------------

* Lead and develop a multi-disciplinary team of Quality Systems, Product Quality, Supplier/Incoming Quality, Quality Control, inspection, technician, and specialist roles.

* Implement planned organization expansion, including Quality Systems leadership, compliance coordination, QC supervision, and temporary integration support, while clarifying accountability across product and system responsibilities.

* Build succession depth and technical capability through coaching, performance management, role clarity, development plans, and targeted cross-training across legacy product and QMS environments.

* Set clear performance expectations and foster a culture of ownership, constructive challenge, timely decision-making, and practical continuous improvement.

* Plan resource needs and manage the site Quality Operations budget, contractor usage, and external support in line with the operating plan.

 
 

**Customer, Supplier, and Compliance Interface**
------------------------------------------------

* Own the Quality Operations response to significant customer issues, quality agreements, customer audits, field escalations, and product-quality communications in partnership with Commercial Quality and Regulatory.

* Provide governance for supplier quality and incoming-quality activities, including risk-based controls, supplier corrective action, change assessment, and escalation of supply continuity risks.
